Title: MXene-modified Sb2Se3@NCR anode for high-performance potassium-ion batteries with enhanced stability and low-temperature tolerance
Abstract: Antimony selenide (Sb<inf>2</inf>Se<inf>3</inf>) is a promising multi-electron reaction electrode material for potassium-ion batteries (PIBs), offering high capacity and potential for grid-scale energy storage. However, its practical application is hindered by severe volume expansion, sluggish kinetics, and polyselenide shuttling. Herein, we propose a novel Sb<inf>2</inf>Se<inf>3</inf> composite anode, Sb<inf>2</inf>Se<inf>3</inf>@NCR/MXene, featuring a fungi-derived nitrogen-doped carbon ribbon (NCR) and an MXene interface modification to enhance electrochemical performance, suppress polyselenide shuttling, and ensure structural integrity. In-situ and ex-situ analyses reveal that the flexible carbon ribbons effectively accommodate volume expansion, while the Ti<inf>3</inf>C<inf>2</inf>O<inf>2</inf> interfacial layer mitigates polyselenide dissolution, leading to stable and high-rate K⁺ storage across a wide temperature range (-20 to 25 °C). Notably, the heterostructure reduces the K+ migration barrier, enabling rapid ion diffusion and significantly improving rate capability - an effect distinct from conventional capacitance-dominated charge storage in low-dimensional electrode materials. As an anode, the Sb<inf>2</inf>Se<inf>3</inf>@NCR/MXene delivers an outstanding 423 mAh g−1 after 100 cycles at 100 mA g−1, while full cells (Sb<inf>2</inf>Se<inf>3</inf>@NCR/MXene//PTCDA) achieve a high reversible capacity of 198.9 mAh g−1 after 100 cycles, retaining 61.8 % capacity and exhibiting excellent performance even at -20 °C. This study introduces a robust interfacial engineering strategy to advance high-performance PIB electrodes, particularly for extreme low-temperature applications. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Mechanochemically and microstructurally intensified kilogram-grade MnO2 for aqueous zinc ion batteries with ultrahigh rate and ultrafast air self-charging
Abstract: Sluggish reaction kinetic, high energy barrier and poor structural stability lead to rapid capacity decay and terrible self-charging properties, becoming major obstacles in using industrial-grade MnO<inf>2</inf> as a cathode in aqueous zinc-ion batteries (AZIBs). Herein, we propose a dual intensification strategy of super liquid membrane reactor (SLMR) treatment + bismuth (Bi) ions modification to achieve efficient and reversible Zn2+ storage and excellent ORR self-charging capability for kilogram-scale industrial MnO<inf>2</inf>. The experiments and theoretical calculations authenticate that SLMR nanosizing and Bi modification increase more active sites, and the newly formed Bi–O bond stabilizes the tunneling structure, greatly improving the conductivity and reversibility and leading to the decreased Zn2+ migration energy barrier. The prepared Bi-MMO manifests an excellent rate performance at an ultrahigh current density of 20 A g-1 and an outstanding energy density of 338 Wh kg-1 and long-term durability, far surpassing the currently reported Mn-based cathodes in AZIBs. Amazingly, the Bi-MMO has a high air self-charging rate 20 times that of MnO<inf>2</inf> owing to its low oxygen adsorption barrier, and the accumulative capacity increased from 183.7 to 1372.8 mAh g-1 after ten cycles. This work advances the development of AZIBs and expands the promising application of MnO<inf>2</inf> in self-charging systems. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.

Title: Evolution of coordinated chemical innovations: A road to chlorine-free magnesium electrolyte system
Abstract: Rechargeable magnesium batteries are recognized as compelling candidates for advanced energy storage technologies, offering economic viability, exceptional safety, and remarkable volumetric energy density. Despite these merits, the deployment of magnesium batteries is hindered by limited insights into solvation dynamics and ion transport within electrolytes. Electrolytes incorporating chloride additives demonstrate efficacy in reducing the passivation layer and achieving higher cycling life. Nevertheless, their corrosive nature poses compatibility challenges with battery components, obstructing scalable commercial adoption. In response, contemporary efforts have shifted toward chlorine-free electrolytes to circumvent these constraints. This comprehensive review critically analyzes Mg-Cl coordination chemistry while advocating for innovative chlorine-free electrolytes. The discussion subsequently evaluates cutting-edge advancements in chlorine-free electrolytes, emphasizing innovative strategies in electrolyte composition (e.g., weakly coordinating anions, non-nucleophilic solvents) to enhance Mg2+ ion transport and interfacial compatibility. Concurrently, research advances related to the interface between chlorine-free electrolytes and anodes are presented. This work establishes actionable guidelines for the next generation of high-performance magnesium batteries. © 2025 Elsevier B.V., All rights reserved.
